## Rationale
The problem this assessment addresses is a near-duplication: commissioned to build a Theory Inventory, the author instead found that one already existed (`three_model_convergence/01_source-analysis/dimension-registry.md`) and was more mature than what was about to be built, invoking CORPUS-SEARCH-RULE.md and ES-005.4 ("search before modelling; if one exists, consume or extend it — never create a second") to justify not building a rival, explicitly naming this as the same defect class recorded elsewhere as G-101/G-68 [S2879]. The gap this closed was methodological/governance rather than conceptual: rather than re-deriving a new theory inventory, the author performed a field-by-field audit of the existing registry against the requested schema, finding most requested safeguards (MD-017's six-way taxonomy, MD-018's non-demoting status chain, a term-collision rule, a Grounding axis, a 13-value status vocabulary, and a non-merging possible_correspondence relation) already enforced [S2879], and isolating exactly five genuine schema gaps: per-concept ID, latest-appearance, implementation (the largest gap — only 18 of 65 mentions reference actual code), dependencies, and open-questions-on-the-entry [S2879]. The rationale for the recommended extension path (rather than a new artifact) is that the batch's own four verification artifacts (V1-V4) were shown to each fill exactly one of those five gaps, revealing that two research lanes — the registry-building `three_model_convergence` lane and the week's gap-discovery lane — had been running in parallel, complementary but previously unconnected [S2879]. A further rationale-relevant self-correction: this same assessment initially measured the registry at "123 concept entries," which a same-day companion document (S2881) corrected by section-boundary analysis to only 27 true concept entries plus 96 file-landmark entries — a four-times-larger true concept-coverage gap than first stated, also explaining why the "Latest appearance" field had appeared absent (file-indexed entries have no "latest" by construction) [S2881]. The author also self-applied the same critique to their own work, reporting that their own gita-candidates register duplicated 9 of 12 sampled terms already in the existing registry, with only 3 terms (independently confirmed via a different route, GR-4) genuinely new [S2879].
